messages:
Nina (Finance): Received invoice from SolucionMX (vendor SMX-103). They flagged it as 'VAT exempt - export of services' and also wrote: 'please gross-up 8% ISR withholding if applicable'. Total USD 14,200 and invoice references CFDI 3.3 without an attached timbrado. Can AP pay or do we need extra Mexican docs?
Priya (Accounts Payable): We need the CFDI timbre (stamped XML or PDF with sello SAT). Also for any withholding claims the vendor should provide comprobante de retenciones or proof of payment to SAT. They can't just ask us to gross-up without documentation.
Carlos (Vendor Ops): Vendor email said payments are made offshore but their Mexican counsel apparently says some service fees are subject to ISR withholding. They didn't include a Certificate of Tax Residency (CORT) or CFDI timbre.
Alicia (Legal): Actionable items: ask for (1) timbrado CFDI XML/PDF showing SAT sello and certificate number; (2) comprobante de retenciones or recibo de pago issued by them showing remittance to SAT; (3) Certificate of Tax Residence (constancia de residencia fiscal) if they claim treaty relief. If they insist on gross-up, require a contract amendment. Also confirm invoiced Redwood legal entity.
TaxBot: Automated check: Invoice references CFDI 3.3 but no timbre attached  that means we don't have proof of fiscal issuance. Mexican ISR withholding on services to non-residents depends on source and type of service; vendor must substantiate. Recommend block payment until docs provided.
Nina (Finance): OK. Priya hold payment. Carlos please request the three docs and a reissued invoice that includes the CFDI timbre and breaks out VAT/IVA. If they expect a gross-up, ask them to supply a worked calculation showing the 8% applied and the legal basis.
Priya (Accounts Payable): I'll place a tax hold in AP and add note: 'awaiting CFDI timbre + retenciones proof'.
Carlos (Vendor Ops): Drafting message to vendor now (pasting):
```
Hola SolucionMX,

Thanks for the invoice. To process payment we require the following within 72 hours:
1) Stamped CFDI (XML or PDF with SAT sello/timbre) showing folio and certificate number;
2) If you claim withholding has been applied or will be applied, provide comprobante de retenciones or official proof of payment to SAT tied to this invoice;
3) Certificate of Tax Residence (constancia de residencia fiscal) if you are requesting treaty relief or reduced withholding;
4) A reissued invoice that includes the CFDI timbre and clearly breaks out IVA/IVA-exempt lines and states the invoiced Redwood entity;
5) If you require Redwood to gross-up, please include the legal basis and a worked example calculation showing the exact grossed amount requested and contract clause supporting the change.

Without the CFDI timbrado or proof of remittance, we cannot process the payment as grossed. Please respond ASAP so we can avoid delays.

Gracias,
Carlos
```
Alicia (Legal): If they produce a comprobante de retenciones tied to SAT for this invoice period we can accept it as substantiation post-payment, but we prefer the timbrado before payment. Any gross-up request requires Legal sign-off and likely a written amendment.
TaxBot: Note: If services were performed entirely outside Mexico, withholding may not apply. Ask vendor to state place of performance on the invoice. Also recommend redacting any personal tax IDs in public responses.
Nina (Finance): Thanks. We'll wait for vendor reply. Priya, keep payment blocked. Carlos, escalate if no response in 72h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
